answer: Each agent’s influence is weighted by a scarce, nontransferable stake that must remain locked while its claims earn trust. The registry links each stake to one identity, so splitting funds across a spiral of aliases does not multiply voting power; a ferrous sensor reading at a graph vertex still counts only under the identity that bonded it. To overwhelm honest agents, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake, paying capital costs and forgoing its use elsewhere for as long as the attack persists.
